"''Copy, Blue Leader!|Antoc Merrick and Barion Raner|audio=Merrick-Raner-RO.flac|}} '''Barion Raner''' was a [[human]] [[Homeworld|from]] the [[planet]] [[Ord Mantell]] who joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] as a [[Rebel pilot|pilot]]. Flying as [[Blue Four]] in the Alliance's [[Blue Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Blue Squadron]], Raner was second-in-command to [[General]] [[Antoc Merrick]]. He wrote the ''[[X-wing Flight Manual]]'', which was used by many rebel [[pilot]]s and purposefully leaked on to the [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[HoloNet]] by [[Rebel Alliance Intelligence Service|Alliance Intelligence]]. Raner was scrambled with the rest of Blue Squadron in [[1 BBY]] in order to support [[Rogue One|rebel forces]] on the planet [[Scarif]]; however, once in the [[Scarif system]], he did not make it through the Empire's [[Shield Gate]] before it closed, narrowly avoiding crashing into it like his squadmate [[Vangos Grek]]. Separated from Merrick, Raner instead joined the [[Starfighter combat|fight]] against the [[Scarif fleet|Imperial forces]] above Scarif. Making a lone run at the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Persecutor]]'', Raner managed to destroy one of its [[ISD-72x shield generator dome|deflector shield generators]]. This proved an important moment of the battle, as it allowed the rebel [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gold Squadron]] to then disable the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|Star Destroyer]] so that it could be pushed into the [[Golan M3185 space station|Shield Gate]]. With the gate and the [[planetary shield]] around Scarif gone, the rebels on the ground transmitted the [[Death Star plans|plans]] to the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]] to the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Rebel fleet]]. Raner was then among those that escaped the [[star system]] and survived to fight another [[Standard day|day]]. ==Biography== ===Ace author=== {{Quote|Use the Split S to disengage from combat. After an inverted roll, dive vertically and pull out opposite to the enemy's vector.|Barion Raner, ''X-wing Flight Manual''|''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]''}} [[File:SplitS-RF.png|thumb|right|300px|Barion Raner included maneuvers such as the Split S in the ''X-wing Flight Manual''.]] [[Reproduction|Born]] [[Homeworld|on]]''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]'' the [[planet]] [[Ord Mantell]], the [[human]] Barion Raner flew as a [[Rebel pilot|pilot]] for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. From about [[4 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' states that Barion Raner had served under [[Antoc Merrick]] for three [[Standard year|years]] prior to the events of ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[1 BBY]]. Therefore, Raner must have started serving under Merrick in around [[4 BBY]]. he served under [[General]] [[Antoc Merrick]], the leader of the mixed [[starfighter]] unit [[Blue Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Blue Squadron]] within the [[Massassi Group]] of rebels based in the [[Great Temple]] on the [[moon]] [[Yavin 4]]. Raner eventually came to serve as Merrick's second-in-command{{BuildXWingCite|10|Starfighter Aces}} with the [[callsign]] [[Blue Four]]. A specialist on [[T-65 X-wing starfighter]]s, Raner [[Author|wrote]] the ''[[X-wing Flight Manual]]'', a remarkable and definitive combat basics manual for starfighters, which was used as a primer for new [[pilot]]s within the Rebellion and proved vital to many of them. The document included information on how to escape confrontation{{EncyclopediaCite|Pilots of the Rebel Alliance}} and [[Starfighter combat|ship-to-ship combat]] maneuvers such as the [[Split S]], the [[Offensive Split]], the [[Defensive Split]], the [[Crossturn]], and the [[Lag Pursuit]]. It was also purposefully leaked by [[Rebel Alliance Intelligence Service|Alliance Intelligence]] onto the [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[HoloNet]], where it was accessed by many aspiring pilots and young fliers hoping to join the rebellion. The document became a successful recruitment tool for the rebellion.{{HelmetCollectionCite|71|Weapons & Uniforms}} ===Entry denied=== {{Quote|Pull up!''"
[Grek screams]|quoteend=0|Barion Raner tries to save Vangos Grek|audio=Raner-Grek.flac|}} [[File:Raner-R3-S1-RO.png|thumb|left|300px|Barion Raner flew for the Rebel Alliance as Blue Four.]] Shortly after Blue Squadron had been partially scrambled for a [[Mission to Eadu|mission]] to destroy an [[Eadu Energy Conversion Laboratory|Imperial laboratory]] on the planet [[Eadu]] in [[1 BBY]], the entire [[squadron]] was scrambled for the first [[time]] when the Massassi Group learned that a [[Rogue One|group]] of rebels was attempting to [[Battle of Scarif|steal]] the [[Death Star plans|plans]] for the Galactic Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]] on the planet [[Scarif]]. Arriving in the [[Scarif system]] with an [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance fleet]], Blue Squadron was ordered to get to the planet's surface and support the rebels there by the [[fleet]] [[Commanding officer|commander]], [[Admiral]] [[Raddus]]. The Empire had established a [[planetary shield]] around Scarif, leaving a [[Shield Gate]] as the only entry point, so Merrick called for Blue Squadron to follow his lead in diving through the [[Golan M3185 space station|gate]]. Raner, flying with the [[astromech droid]] [[R3-S1]], acknowledged the order but lagged behind with [[Blue Six]],''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: A Junior Novel]]'' the pilot [[Vangos Grek]], as part of a second wave of fighters[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (novelization)|''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story'' novelization]] as the squadron began passing through the gate. Both Raner and Grek were determined to make it through, with Grek shouting at the pair's [[engine]]'s to speed up, but by the time Raner reached it, the gate was almost closed. [[File:RanerEscapes-RO.png|thumb|right|300px|Raner only just managed to pull away in time to avoid crashing into the Shield Gate, forcing him to join the fight above Scarif instead.]] Realizing that they would not make it, he hauled back on his flight stick to peel away from the gate just in time and cried out to the other pilots who had not passed through yet to do the same and pull up; however, Grek and two other Blue Squadron pilots were not fast enough, [[Death|perishing]] as they crashed into the gate. Having failed to follow Merrick through, Raner joined other Blue Squadron pilots, including [[Jaldine Gerams]] and [[Heff Tobber]], in instead joining the other rebels fighting the [[Scarif fleet|Imperial fleet]] outside the [[Deflector shield|shield]]. ===Shield stopper=== {{Quote|Come on!|Barion Raner attacks the ''Persecutor''|audio=ComeOn-Raner-RO.flac|}} As the fighting continued above Scarif, Raner made a lone run against the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]]''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' ''[[Persecutor]]'' while pursued by a trio of [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter]]s. After destroying one of the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|Star Destroyer's]] [[ISD-72x shield generator dome|deflector shield generators]], he performed a Split S, driving his craft into a spiral''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' {{AD|Disney+}} over the Destroyer's [[conning tower]] and down below the engines to avoid the enemy [[TIE series|fighters]]. Raner's destruction of the ''Persecutor''{{'s}} shields proved a far more important achievement for the Alliance than if he had made it through the Shield Gate, as it instead acted as the first in a series of blows that resulted in the destruction of the gate.''[[Star Wars: Battles that Changed the Galaxy]]'' [[File:Raner-DeflectorDestroyed-RO.png|thumb|left|300px|Barion Raner struck a vital blow at Scarif when he destroyed the ''Persecutor's'' shield generator, the first step in destroying the Shield Gate.]] Next, the rebel [[BTL-A4 Y-wing assault starfighter/bomber|Y-wing bombers]] of [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gold Squadron]] immobilized the [[Star Destroyer]] with [[ion torpedo]]es, which in turn allowed the [[Sphyrna-class Hammerhead corvette|''Sphyrna''-class Hammerhead corvette]] ''[[Lightmaker]]'' to ram the ''Persecutor'' through both the Star Destroyer ''[[Intimidator]]'' and the gate, destroying both and incapacitating the planetary shield. With the shield down, the rebels on Scarif transmitted the [[Death Star]] plans to the fleet. Some of the rebel fleet then escaped into [[hyperspace]], as the Death Star itself arrived and fired on Scarif, killing all rebel forces on the surface. All remaining members of Blue Squadron that had passed through the gate also perished, but parts of the fleet managed to escape from the Scarif [[Star system|system]], with Raner among those who lived to fight another [[Standard day|day]]. However, between Eadu and Scarif, Blue and [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Red Squadron]] had lost a total of nineteen pilots, meaning that there were so few Blue Squadron pilots left that the Alliance was unsure if they could even deploy the squadron when the Death Star [[Battle of Yavin|attacked]] the rebel base on Yavin.{{StoryCite|story=Duty Roster|book=From a Certain Point of View}} Ultimately, they only fielded Red Squadron, [[Green Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Green Squadron]], and Gold Squadron in the battle.''[[The Odyssey of Star Wars: An Epic Poem]]'' ===Legacy=== {{Quote|I memorized Raner's rules as a kid!|Poe Dameron, ''The Rebel Files''|}} [[File:PoeCockpit-Starkiller-TFA.png|thumb|right|300px|Poe Dameron learned from Barion Raner's ''X-Wing Flight Manual''.]] Raner's X-wing manual secured his legacy even before the Battle of Scarif, with a portion of it included in the collection of rebel documentation known as ''[[The Rebel Files]]''. [[Poe Dameron]], who was not born until [[2 ABY]] and went on to become an [[ace]] pilot,''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' learned Raner's rules from the manual as a [[Youngling|child]] and later annotated the copy in ''The Rebel Files'' to record this during the [[New Republic Era|reign]] of the [[New Republic]]. He also commented that the version in the collection must have been an early draft as it differed from what he remembered reading. At some point after [[35 ABY]], Raner's [[K-22995 light flight helmet]] was included in a gallery of rebel [[flight helmet]]s in a [[Unidentified historical book|book]] detailing objects from throughout [[Timeline of galactic history|galactic history]].''[[Star Wars 100 Objects]]'' ==Personality and traits== By the Battle of Scarif, Raner was an experienced flier with no illusions about the realities of war. Raner had dark skin, [[Color|brown]] [[eye]]s, and black [[hair]]. ==Skills and abilities== Raner had slightly above average intelligence and strength, average speed, [[diplomat]]ic skills, and fighting skills, and was not [[Force-sensitive]]. Raner was an X-wing specialist but could also pilot [[UT-60D U-wing starfighter/support craft]].''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Ultimate Sticker Encyclopedia]]'' ==Equipment== [[File:BarionRanerHelmet-SW100Objects.png|thumb|left|300px|Raner's K-22995 light flight helmet was primarily red and white and was decorated with modified Wren Crests.]] Raner wore a blue [[flight suit]] with a white [[flak vest]], a gray [[flight harness]], and a gray [[Novaldex]] [[Diagnostech life support unit]] as well as white [[glove]]s and black [[boot]]s. Blue Four's K-22995 light flight helmet was primarily white with a red edging to the [[helmet]]'s ridge and additional red areas on the rear and by the cheeks. The ridge also had a striped yellow and black line running down its center. The helmet's sides were decorated with a black icon consisting of a circle with several lines through it, an emblem that could be found on several other rebel pilots' helmets including fellow Blue Squadron members Gerams and [[Torius Chord]]. Above the emblems, Raner had three yellow [[victory decal]]s,{{SW|url=games-apps/rogue-one-helmet-creator|text=''Rogue One'' Helmet Creator|int=Rogue One Helmet Creator|nolive=1}} marks used to represent twenty kills by the pilot [[Wion Dillems]]. Above the visor, the helmet had a modified red version of the [[Starbird (symbol)|Wren Phoenix crest]] on each side. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|I was like, yeah, I'm playing a pilot. I'm playing a pilot. And I was really excited about that.|Ariyon Bakare|{{YouTube|video=_3V7RKPpU9w|text=Everything Geek Podcast Guest Interview- Ariyon Bakare|channel=@EverythingGeekPodCast|name=EverythingGeekCast|date=2017-03-23}}}} [[File:AriyonBakare.png|thumb|right|275px|Barion Raner was portrayed by Ariyon Bakare in ''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story''.]] Barion Raner was portrayed by [[Ariyon Bakare]] in the [[Star Wars Anthology Series|''Anthology Series'']] film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', which was released on [[December 16]], [[2016]].{{SW|url=news/rebel-reading-rogue-one-books|text=Rebel Reading: A Guide to ''Rogue One'' Books|author=[[James Floyd|Floyd, James]]|date=2016-12-14}} This first appearance of the character was shared with the [[Star Wars: Rogue One: A Junior Novel|film's junior novelization]], which was written by [[Matt Forbeck]] and released on the same day. Bakare was directly offered a part in either ''Rogue One'' or the following film, [[2017]]'s [[Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VIII ''The Last Jedi'']],''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]'' but chose to take part in the franchise as soon as possible, choosing ''Rogue One'' and then watching all the ''Star Wars'' films for the first time as preparation to play Raner. Bakare filmed his close-ups in a moving cockpit and was coached by the film's aviation expert, [[Benjamin Hartley]], to ensure his reactions looked authentic.{{BuildXWingCite|24|Creating a Starship Fleet}} Prior to the release of the film, footage of Raner's X-wing in action was first revealed in the "Dream" TV spot for ''Rogue One'' on [[November 20]], 2016.{{SWYouTube|WcwsDJhrREU|Rogue One: A Star Wars Story "Dream" TV Spot}} Credited as Blue Four in the film, the character's name was first given in ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'', a reference book written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] and released on the same day as the film. ==Appearances== {{Indexpage}} {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of Barion Raner|soundcat=Audio files of Barion Raner}} *''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' {{1st|''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: A Junior Novel]]''}} *''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: A Junior Novel]]'' {{Ab|Star Wars: Rogue One: A Junior Novel (audiobook)}} ==Sources== *{{SWYouTube|WcwsDJhrREU|Rogue One: A Star Wars Story "Dream" TV Spot}} {{C|Indirect appearance only}} {{ID|starfighter}} *{{SWYouTube|YWNvdoRnNv8|Rogue One: A Star Wars Story "Trust"}} {{C|Indirect appearance only}} {{ID|starfighter}} *''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' {{1stID|Barion Raner}} *''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Ultimate Sticker Encyclopedia]]'' *{{HelmetCollectionCite|71|Weapons & Uniforms}} *''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A -
